schedule: before 9am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Fallback: everything non-major for the shipped backend plugin — the version catalog, the plugin build and the Gradle wrapper — in one PR. This is the product, so it stays visible and reviewed
Fallback: everything non-major for the published plugin library and the repo root in one PR

The test-app is a vendored copy of the GZAC templates, front and back: 94 of its ~111 npm packages arrived with the template, and test-app/backend/gradle.properties is the template's own plugin-version list. These are the versions a real Valtimo application runs. Bumping them on our own says nothing about whether Valtimo supports the result, and it costs the harness the very thing it is for — resembling a real deployment. So the whole directory is tracked on the dependency dashboard and moves as part of a Valtimo bump, not on a schedule. The shipped plugin is what gets the reviewed, scheduled PRs

The exceptions in that file that are ours rather than the template's: the plugin's own JSONata runtime and the Playwright E2E suite. Grouped with the rest of the frontend so they keep updating normally

The pnpm overrides are CVE floors, not pins — raising a floor that nothing violates is pure churn, so keep them off the PR queue. A real advisory still opens a PR immediately via vulnerabilityAlerts, which ignores dashboard approval
Container images across compose, Dockerfiles and the Helm chart in one PR

Automerge the digest re-pins that helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests produces — same tag, new SHA, so there is nothing to read, and every workflow is exercised by the CI run on the branch. Version changes are excluded and still get reviewed

gradle, java, node, pnpm and helm are each declared in several places — .mise.toml, the Gradle wrapper, package.json engines, the workflows — and must not drift apart. Matched on depName because the packageName differs per manager (gradle/gradle-distributions, actions/node-versions, helm/helm). The explicit flags stop this rule inheriting automerge or dashboard gating from the file-scoped rules above, which it pulls deps out of
oxlint and oxfmt are declared in both .mise.toml and package.json — a drift between the two makes the local run and the CI format/lint gate disagree

Angular stays visible, unlike the rest of the template stack, because the plugin's own peerDependencies permit a range here (>=19.2.8 <20) rather than an exact version — so a 19.x update is inside the compatibility we publish. The major is dictated by Valtimo and falls under the major gate below

Non-major Gradle updates already travel together in `backend dependencies`; these four rules only shape the majors, so that a major Spring Boot / Kotlin / Testcontainers / build-plugin bump is one dashboard entry instead of one per module and per version source

The published library's peer ranges are a hand-set compatibility contract that is recorded in COMPATIBILITY.md, not something to widen automatically — a widened range would claim support for a Valtimo/Angular version nobody has tested. The versions actually installed here are covered by the devDependencies of the same package

The Form.io stylesheets are two deliberately different Font Awesome majors loaded from a CDN behind SRI hashes; a version bump needs the integrity hash recomputed by hand, so Renovate does not own them

Libraries whose version Valtimo dictates rather than us. The plugin's own peerDependencies pin these to an EXACT version (formiojs 4.19.5, carbon-components-angular 5.57.6, @formio/angular 7.0.0) because that is what the Valtimo frontend loads — so an independent bump would break the contract we publish, whatever CI says. They stay on the dependency dashboard and are re-pinned by hand as part of a Valtimo bump. Deliberately NOT folded into the `valtimo` group: that group is the direct platform dependencies only

Majors are coordinated work here — nearly all of them are dictated by the Valtimo platform. List them on the dependency dashboard (issue #50) and open a PR only when one is ticked. Valtimo itself is exempted by the rule below

The direct Valtimo platform dependencies, and only those — backend modules and frontend packages, which are one version and must move in lockstep. A Valtimo bump is a potentially large change, so it always arrives as its own PR, major included, rather than waiting on the dashboard. It is a starting point, not a mergeable change: run the update-valtimo skill on it to review the changelog, re-pin the template libraries above and update COMPATIBILITY.md. Listed last so it overrides the major gate, and never automerged
